architecture.mechanism: Suppress the correctable residual error component and swap labels without decoding the payload — deliberately channel the "correctable" fraction of a damaging agent onto a sacrificial, swappable carrier element so the residual stream is left suppressed, protected internals stay clean, and the carrier can be exchanged without altering the underlying system.
architecture.intervention: Fit a slip-in sacrificial "header" cartridge (no pressure-boundary welding, matched to existing flash-vessel/cyclone/injection-header geometry) seeded with calcite/silica nucleation sites and pH-modulating dosing points; flashed brine below 180°C with calcium up to 900 mg/L is held in a controlled local-supersaturation window so scale precipitates preferentially onto the cartridge instead of flash-vessel internals, cyclones, or injection headers; the cartridge is swapped during the 4-day annual outage with on-site equipment, plus a verification mode that checks cartridge capture and internal cleanliness end-to-end.
architecture.expected_effect: The 6–11% quarterly thermal-output loss is reduced because heat-transfer and flow surfaces stay largely free of calcite/silica gel beyond the current 45–60 day cycle; deposition is concentrated on a consumable element; service fits the 4-day outage with no pressure-boundary welding; tolerance to 900 mg/L calcium is retained by keeping the brine in the seeded "correctable" deposition regime.
architecture.falsification_test: Side-stream pilot on one of the 12 wells: split flashed brine between a seeded sacrificial-cartridge leg and an unseeded blank leg of identical geometry at the same temperature (<180°C) and calcium level (up to 900 mg/L); over 60 days weigh scale on the cartridge versus flash-vessel/cyclone/injection-header coupons and track heat-transfer coefficient and pressure drop. The mechanism is falsified if the seeded leg does not capture a substantially larger share of the scale and leave internals measurably cleaner, or if the cartridge swap cannot be completed within the 4-day outage using on-site equipment.
